data.title: Value Proposition Canvas — kadence
body: # Value Proposition Canvas — kadence
- **Date:** 2026-09-16 · **Replaces:** the 2026-09-02 canvas (Ukrainian, segment "developer in a terminal with an agent", product at 0.1a)

- **Segment:** one account type, two people in it — a team of **3–8 developers on shared repositories, ≥ 2 using coding agents daily** ([strategy §1](DOC-35)). Canvas A is the **buyer**, the tech lead who adds `.kadence/`. Canvas B is the **second author**, the developer whose agent reads what the lead wrote. The North Star lives in B: a repository only counts once a second author writes.
- **Fit level tested:** problem–solution. Nothing here reaches product–market fit; that needs behaviour, and there are 0 external users.

- **Evidence:** **no interviews** (Probe B: 0 held as of today). What exists — one unsolicited tech-lead conversation ([tech-lead feedback](tech-lead-feedback-2026-09-10.md), n = 1); public issues from Beads and Backlog.md users ([discovery verdict](DOC-45)); Probe A on merge conflicts; the vendors' own docs; the product as it ships (the product inventory of 2026-09-16, see Sources).

- **Labels:** **Fact** (measured, in the code, or stated by a primary source) · **Inference** (our reading) · **Assumption** (unevidenced, load-bearing). A canvas without interviews is a hypothesis sheet; every rank below is ours, not the customer's.
- **Value map scope:** features in **0.4.1 on npm**. Working-tree features not yet published are marked *(unreleased)* and never carry a fit on their own.
> Method: Strategyzer Value Proposition Canvas (Osterwalder, Pigneur et al., *Value Proposition Design*, 2014).
## What changed since 2026-09-02
| Then | Now | Why |

| Segment: a solo developer with an agent | Team of 3–8; buyer = tech lead; second author = developer | Claude Code Auto Memory and Tasks now serve the solo case; they are machine-local ([Claude Code memory docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory), accessed 2026-09-16) |
| Main unique pain: merge conflicts, severity unknown | Conflicts measured: **15%** of 130 repos, about **one merge in two hundred** — real but rare. Proof, not headline | [Probe A](DOC-55) |
| Strong fit: velocity from the journal | Velocity demoted to "present, not advertised": 0 requests across 1,076 Beads issues and Backlog.md's history | [discovery verdict §3](DOC-45) |
| Gap: no board (TUI deferred) | TUI kanban, `ready`, `prime`, claims, criteria, milestones, reports, HTML/Markdown export all ship | inventory §2 |
| No evidence from the segment | One tech lead: drifting state is real, but it is caused by **attention**, not storage | tech-lead feedback |
## Canvas A — the tech lead (buyer)
**Who:** tech lead, staff/senior or founding engineer; writes `CLAUDE.md`; can add a directory to the repo alone. Runs a team where several people and several agents touch the same work.
### A1. Jobs (ranked by our estimate)
| # | Job | Type | Importance | Evidence |

| A-J1 | When someone else (a person or their agent) picks up work I or my agent started, make sure they know what was tried, decided and blocked — without me re-explaining | functional | **high** | **Inference** from the ICP job statement; **Fact** that the category exists: 482,304 public repos with a root `AGENTS.md`, 3,272 with Beads, 458 with Backlog.md (discovery verdict §1, 2026-09-08) |

| A-J2 | Know which important work nobody is watching | functional | **high** | **Fact (n = 1):** "drifting state happens because everyone stops watching some part of the work that actually matters" (tech-lead feedback, translated) |

| A-J3 | Keep a rejected approach from coming back in a later session or from another teammate's agent | functional | high | **Inference** from triggers in strategy §1 ("a rejected approach came back"); **Assumption** that it recurs often enough to act on |

| A-J4 | Control quality of agent output — know who used which agent and how it went | functional / social | medium | **Fact (n = 1):** "you need to know who uses which AI and improve based on that" (tech-lead feedback, translated) |
| A-J5 | Show stakeholders where the work stands without making them open a terminal | social | medium | **Inference**; **Assumption** that the ICP's manager is not already served by Jira/Linear |
| A-J6 | Adopt a tool without a security review, an account or a server to run | functional | medium | **Inference** from the ICP "Not for: > 20 developers asking for SSO" |

| A-J7 | Look competent to the team: pick a tool that does not become a chore | emotional | medium | **Fact** that the opposite happened elsewhere: "I spend a bunch of time caring for beads itself instead of doing beads" (Beads issue, 17 reactions, discovery verdict §2) |
### A2. Pains (severity × frequency, our estimate)
| # | Pain | Rating | Evidence |

| A-P1 | Context is re-explained at every handoff between people, machines and agent vendors; vendor memory does not travel | **high × daily** | **Fact:** Claude Code auto memory "is machine-local … Files are not shared across machines or cloud environments" ([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory), accessed 2026-09-16). **Fact:** ai-memory's 6,965 stars for cross-vendor handoff (GitHub API, 2026-09-16). **Assumption:** the ICP feels it strongly enough to install something — Probe B |
| A-P2 | Important work silently goes unattended (stalled, unowned, stale claims) | **high × weekly** | **Fact (n = 1)**, tech-lead feedback |

| A-P3 | Too many signals for one head — "how many of those signals fit in your head" | high × daily | **Fact (n = 1)**; **Inference:** any new tool adds signals, so this pain also works *against* adoption |

| A-P4 | Tracker upkeep becomes its own job: daemons, migrations, database corruption | high × at upgrade | **Fact:** Beads issues "Moving to dolt pretty much made beads unusable for me" (38 reactions, closed 2026-05-22) and "Beads feels painful to use" (17); Beads v1.3.0 applies ~28 schema migrations on first run ([release notes](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/releases/tag/v1.3.0), accessed 2026-09-16) |

| A-P5 | Tasks and code drift apart: issue state lives outside the commit, branch or PR | medium × weekly | **Fact:** "code changes and issue updates could be in the same commit, same branch, same PR" — lost after Beads moved to Dolt (Beads issue, 4 reactions) |

| A-P6 | Concurrent writes collide: two tasks get the same ID, two agents claim one task | medium × rare, but silent | **Fact:** Backlog.md user "hit this in production twice"; the collision-free ID proposal was closed *not planned* 2026-07-10 ([#711](https://github.com/MrLesk/Backlog.md/issues/711), accessed 2026-09-16). **Fact:** Probe A, ~1 merge in 200 |
| A-P7 | Cannot tell which model produced which outcome | medium × per review | **Fact (n = 1)**; nobody in the category records it |
| A-P8 | A drift claim over-promises: a board that is "never out of date" is still wrong when nobody writes to it | medium × at pilot | **Fact:** tech-lead feedback, Finding 1 |
### A3. Gains
| # | Gain | Class | Evidence |

| A-G1 | A teammate's agent starts a session already knowing decisions in force and what is ready | **must-have** | **Inference** from A-J1; **Fact** that the pattern is the category norm (`bd prime`, Backlog.md overview) |
| A-G2 | One short list of what needs a human look | **must-have** | **Fact (n = 1)** |
| A-G3 | Nothing to host, nothing to migrate, nothing to babysit | expected | **Fact:** A-P4 complaints |
| A-G4 | History that survives `git checkout` and travels in the same PR as the code | desired | **Fact:** Beads users' stated loss (A-P5) |
| A-G5 | Per-agent / per-model quality visible | desired | **Fact (n = 1)**; **Assumption** that it is wanted beyond this one lead, and does not become surveillance ([assumptions map #12](DOC-39)) |
| A-G6 | A page to send a manager | nice-to-have | **Assumption** |
| A-G7 | Sprint velocity and cost | unexpected, not a pull | **Fact:** 0 requests in the category |
## Canvas B — the second author (developer on the team)
**Who:** a developer on the same repository who did not choose kadence. Uses Claude Code, Cursor or Codex. Meets the tool when their agent runs `prime` or when the lead asks them to claim a task.
### B1. Jobs
| # | Job | Importance | Evidence |
| B-J1 | Start a session on work someone else started and get going without a meeting | **high** | **Inference** (mirror of A-J1) |

| B-J2 | Pick the next thing to do without stepping on a teammate or their agent | **high** | **Fact:** "two agents claim the same task before either pushes" (Backlog.md [#937](https://github.com/MrLesk/Backlog.md/issues/937), open, accessed 2026-09-16) |
| B-J3 | Record what I decided or learned so nobody asks me again | medium | **Assumption** — the second author may not care about the lead's record |

| B-J4 | Keep my own flow: stay in the editor and terminal, not in another tool | **high** | **Inference**; **Fact** that Backlog.md now defaults to CLI instructions over MCP ([README](https://github.com/MrLesk/Backlog.md), accessed 2026-09-16) |
| B-J5 | Show the work was done properly (criteria met) without writing a report | medium | **Inference** |
### B2. Pains
| # | Pain | Rating | Evidence |
| B-P1 | Another tool the lead picked: new commands, new rituals, nothing in it for me | **high × at adoption** | **Assumption**, and the North Star's biggest risk (N2 in strategy §6, risk 7.2) |
| B-P2 | My agent repeats a path the team already rejected | high × weekly | **Inference**; **Assumption** on frequency |
| B-P3 | Merge conflicts or duplicate IDs in task files after a branch lands | medium × rare | **Fact:** Probe A (15% of repos, ~1 in 200 merges) |
| B-P4 | Agent context bloated by tracker output | medium × every call | **Fact:** Beads measured `bd ready --json` at 454,021 B on a 16k-bead store before `--brief` (v1.3.0 notes) |
| B-P5 | Setup friction: runtime, OS, package manager | medium × once | **Fact:** kadence needs Node ≥ 20, no Windows CI, no binary (inventory §4) |
### B3. Gains
| # | Gain | Class | Evidence |
| B-G1 | `ready` tells me and my agent what is free to take | **must-have** | **Fact:** `bd ready` is Beads' most-used command (feature adoption, 2026-09-09) |
| B-G2 | Zero extra steps: my agent writes and reads the journal for me | **must-have** | **Assumption** |
| B-G3 | My work is attributed to me, my agent's to my agent | desired | **Inference** |
| B-G4 | Nothing to resolve after a merge | expected once experienced | **Fact** that it is possible (integration test) |
## Value map — current features only
### Products and services

A CLI (`kadence`, 0.4.1, 76 KB packed, one runtime dependency loaded only by the TUI) that keeps a team's tasks, decisions, notes and claims as **append-only JSON events** in `.kadence/events/`, committed with the code. Around it: an agent contract (`--json`, `schema --json`, 15 error codes), a session preamble (`prime` + `init --hooks`), a TUI kanban, reports, static HTML/Markdown export, and a separate one-way GitHub publish package. No server, no account, no network in the core. *(Unreleased: `report burndown|velocity|workload`, `report <name> --html`, `report --list`.)*
### Pain relievers
| Pain | Reliever (shipped) | Strength | Label |

| A-P1 context re-explained | `prime` (≤ 40 lines, ≤ 3 KB, under test) at `SessionStart`; `decision add --why --rejected --supersedes`; `note`; `task show --json` with history, decisions, docs, notes, claim (982 B per task; 304 B with `--summary`); one section in both `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, so every vendor reads the same thing | strong in mechanism | **Fact** (built, measured); relief **Assumption** until a second author uses it |
| A-P2 unattended work | `report attention`: `stalled`, `unowned`, `stale_claim`, `dead_blocker`; one attention line inside `prime` | partial — pull only | **Fact** (0.4.4, 0.5 ms over 10k events) |
| A-P3 signal overload | `prime` is capped; attention prints only when there is something to say; no notifications by design | partial | **Fact** (design); **Inference** that fewer signals help |
| A-P4 upkeep | no daemon, no database, no server, no migrations of stored state (state is folded; `state.json` is a disposable cache, I6); `compact` for size | **strong** | **Fact** |
| A-P5 tasks drift from code | events are files in the working tree, in the same commit and PR; `task list --branch` scopes to a branch (3–20× narrower) | **strong** | **Fact** |

| A-P6 collisions | ULID identity, `KAD-N` derived and never stored (I7); merge of three branches in every order gives identical state; claims are events — a double claim reads `contested`, never lost | **strong** for IDs and edits; partial for claims (no lock, visible after merge) | **Fact** |
| A-P7 which model did the work | `source` human/agent on every event, comment and decision — **not** the model | weak | **Fact**; deliberately deferred (tech-lead feedback, Finding 3) |
| A-P8 over-promise | wording: "the board cannot drift from *the journal*; it only knows what gets written to it" | messaging, not a feature | **Fact** (strategy §1) |
| B-P2 repeating rejected paths | `--rejected` kept on decisions; `prime` lists decisions in force | medium | **Assumption** that agents honour it |
| B-P3 merge conflicts | append-only, one file per event | **strong** | **Fact** |
| B-P4 context bloat | `--fields`, `--summary`, narrow `ready --json` (7 fields incl. `labels`) | strong | **Fact:** 200-task board 130,799 B → 11,015 B with `--fields` |
| B-P5 setup | `npx`/npm, 65 ms start, shell completion | partial | **Fact**: Node ≥ 20 remains a barrier |
### Gain creators
| Gain | Creator (shipped) | Label |
| A-G1 agent starts informed | `prime` + hook; decisions in force; last 5 notes | **Fact** (built) |
| A-G2 one list for a human | `report attention`; `stats` (blockers, contested claims) | **Fact** |
| A-G3 nothing to babysit | zero-server, zero-dependency core; 200 ms budget enforced in tests | **Fact** |
| A-G4 history in git | `git checkout` of any commit folds that day's board; `sprint burndown` rebuilt for any day | **Fact** |
| A-G5 per-agent quality | `source` split only; flow reports (cycle time p50/p85/p95) are per team, not per agent | **Fact**: not delivered |
| A-G6 page for a manager | `board export --html` (self-contained, no requests), `--md --readme`; `@kadence/github publish` one-way | **Fact** (experiments with kill conditions) |
| A-G7 velocity | `sprint close`, `report flow`, `report cfd`; *(unreleased)* velocity as low/median/high | **Fact** |
| B-G1 what is free | `ready` (unblocked, unclaimed, not started; priority then age); `task claim` with no argument takes the top | **Fact** |
| B-G2 zero extra steps | agent-first CLI and hook; `KADENCE_SOURCE=agent` | partial — **someone still has to write**; nothing is captured automatically |
| B-G3 attribution | git `user.email` as actor + `source` | **Fact** |
| B-G4 nothing to resolve | conflict-free merge by construction | **Fact** |
## Fit
| Customer element | Our answer | Fit | Why |

| A-P1 / A-J1 context across people and vendors | `prime`, decisions, notes, `task show --json`, shared agent files | **Strong mechanism, unproven pain** | Vendor memory is machine-local by its own docs — the gap is real. Whether a 3–8 team pays the adoption cost for it is Probe B |
| A-P4 upkeep / A-G3 | no server, no DB, no daemon | **Strong** | Directly answers the category leader's loudest complaints. Evidence is from Beads users, not yet from our ICP |
| A-P5 tasks in the commit / A-G4 | events as files in the working tree | **Strong** | Unique among the agent-first trackers now that Beads' source of truth is Dolt |
| A-P6 / B-P3 collisions | ULID + append-only | **Strong but low frequency** | ~1 merge in 200. Proof point for switchers, not a headline |

| B-J2 / B-G1 next task without collisions | `ready` + `claim` (contested, not locked) | **Partial** | Parity with Beads/Backlog.md on `ready`; weaker on real-time exclusion (Beads now has leases and compare-and-set) |
| A-P2 / A-G2 unattended work | `report attention` + `prime` line | **Partial** | Answers the *question* the tech lead asked; it is pull-only, so the lead still has to look |
| A-P3 signal overload | capped output | **Weak** | Every added tool is also a signal source |
| A-J4 / A-P7 / A-G5 which agent, how well | `source` only | **Absent** | Deferred on purpose (contract and surveillance risk) |
| A-J5 / A-G6 stakeholder view | static HTML/MD, GitHub publish | **Partial** | Snapshot, not live; kill condition "nobody opens it twice" untested |
| B-P1 / B-G2 second author's cost | agent does the writing | **Unknown** | The North Star rests here and there is no data |
## Pains kadence does not relieve
Stated plainly so no pitch implies otherwise.

1. **Drift caused by attention.** Append-only removes drift between the board and the journal, not between the journal and reality. A task nobody touches for three weeks folds into a correct board and a wrong picture. `report attention` names it only if someone runs it or reads `prime`. There is no push, no notification, no daemon — a deliberate boundary ([context-handoff](DOC-42), strategy §8). **Fact.**

2. **Work that is never written down.** kadence captures nothing by itself. ai-memory captures prompts and tool calls through lifecycle hooks "silently" ([README](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory), accessed 2026-09-16); kadence's only hook runs `prime`, which reads. If the second author's agent does not write, the journal is empty. **Fact** (mechanism) / **Assumption** (whether agents write reliably when instructed).
3. **Which model did the work, and how well.** No model name is recorded anywhere. **Fact.**
4. **Signal overload.** kadence can shorten what it prints; it cannot shrink what a lead has to hold in their head. **Inference.**
5. **Real-time exclusion between machines.** Two machines can claim the same task before either pushes; kadence shows it after the merge. **Fact** (ADR-011).
6. **Semantic recall over everything an agent saw.** Not a goal; the memory-for-agents projects own that axis. **Fact** (discovery verdict, "not a memory product").
7. **Live visibility for people who never open the repo.** Static export and one-way GitHub publish only; no hosted view, no two-way sync. **Fact** (non-goal).
8. **Teams without Node ≥ 20 or on native Windows.** No binary, no Windows CI. **Fact** (G4).
9. **Enforcing agent permissions or impact policy.** Labels can record intent (`impact-critical`); enforcement belongs to the harness. **Fact** (tech-lead feedback, Finding 4).
## Verdict

**Problem–solution fit: plausible on mechanism, unverified on pain.** The picture inverted since 2026-09-02. Then the unique features faced unconfirmed pains and the confirmed pains were already solved by others. Now the product has caught up on table stakes (board, `ready`, claims, criteria), and its distinctive properties — plain files in the commit, no server, merge without resolution — answer pains that **category users stated in public**. They do not come from our ICP, and there are no interviews.

The strongest unaddressed element is the one the only tech lead we heard raised: **attention**. kadence can make unattended work *visible* when someone looks; it cannot make anyone look. If Probe B hears attention more than context loss, the canvas's centre moves from `prime` to `report attention`, and the journal becomes the substrate rather than the product (tech-lead feedback, "What would make this reading wrong").
## Top unaddressed items, for Probe B
1. **B-P1: does a second author write without being pushed?** The North Star depends on it; nothing in the value map addresses the second author's own motive. Ask pilots at day 7 and day 14.
2. **A-P2 vs A-P1: which pain comes first, unprompted?** The Oct 19 gate decides between them.
3. **Automatic capture (item 2 above).** If interviewees describe "we forget to write it down", the explicit-write model is a weakness, not a virtue.
4. **A-P7: per-model quality.** Record whether any interviewee raises it without a hook.
